evidence.exact_quote: Run Graph is the canonical graph and lineage inspection surface for orchestrated execution. Graph nodes are runtime nodes rather than tiers; lineage spans graph generations; blocked, recovery, promotion, and corroboration state appears in graph detail when it belongs to the selected node or related lineage object.

items.impact: The canonical surface, node identity, generation lineage, and related runtime-detail scope are explicit enough to constrain the owner boundary.
items.statement: Run Graph is explicitly defined as the canonical graph and lineage inspection projection over runtime nodes and graph generations, rather than a tier authority.
items.title: Canonical Run Graph scope is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - Access pivots disclose confidence, health_state, stale_window_expires_at_utc, and source before Open App or Open Container actions.

items.impact: A builder must invent scheme, origin, target-validation, confirmation, permission-denial, and network-failure behavior for URLs and container pivots, risking unsafe opens or inconsistent blocked states.
items.statement: Host access pivots disclose confidence and health but do not define an executable validation and failure contract for untrusted dynamic URLs, schemes, origins, permission denial, or offline targets.
items.title: Host access pivots lack target-safety semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Run Graph distinguishes active run truth from focused run context. active_run_id names live runtime truth; focused_run_id and focus_mode = live | historical name the selected run, page state, and Historical Run Mode behavior across Orchestrator tabs.

items.impact: The specification prevents a selected historical run from being presented as current runtime truth and gives cross-tab consumers a shared focus model.
items.statement: Active runtime identity and user-selected run focus are explicitly separate, with live and historical modes constrained by their relationship.
items.title: Active and focused run truth are separated

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Run Graph uses one shared destination payload for search results, command-palette results, widget drill-downs, recovery links, resume URLs, artifact opens, subject-open semantics, and cross-surface pivots. Navigation preserves target identity and context instead of switching tabs with an approximate target.

items.impact: Different callers can preserve different subsets of identity, filters, focus, and back-stack state while all claiming to use the shared payload, making route fidelity non-falsifiable.
items.statement: The shared destination concept enumerates callers and desired fidelity but does not define the payload fields, required-by-object rules, versioning, conflict precedence, or invalid-target result semantics.
items.title: Shared deep-link payload is not field-complete

evidence.exact_quote: - Large graphs use virtualization, culling, caching, throttled updates, level-of-detail reduction, and lineage-focused defaults.

items.impact: Implementations may satisfy the named techniques while freezing, dropping updates, producing inaccessible low-detail states, or exhausting memory at realistic graph sizes.
items.statement: The graph names scaling techniques but supplies no node/edge thresholds, frame or interaction budgets, memory bounds, update-lag limits, degradation order, or measurable large-graph fixture.
items.title: Large-graph behavior has no quantitative bounds

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Node detail exposes requested/effective provider, model, effort, persona, account, usage, cost, worker policy, retry/review/promotion state, lane, worktree, snapshot, linked evidence, artifacts, review refs, corroboration refs, graph patch refs, recovery refs, blocked episode refs, and promotion refs. Evidence and artifact links deep-link to Evidence with target selection or filtering applied.

items.impact: Account, cost, repository, worktree, snapshot, and artifact metadata can be overexposed or inconsistently redacted, and the UI has no required inaccessible/hidden-state explanation.
items.statement: The inspector defines a rich disclosure set but no field-level permission, redaction, privacy-lifecycle, localization, or accessibility contract for sensitive and unavailable values.
items.title: Inspector disclosure policy is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Run Graph data-source joins retarget away from tier_id and toward node_id, attempt_id, blocked episode, generation, lane, artifact, and provider platform identity. Field-name modernization is insufficient unless scope is also modernized to the runtime identities that own execution truth.

items.impact: Consumers have an explicit rule preventing cosmetic field renames from preserving tier-era authority underneath the projection.
items.statement: Runtime join authority is explicitly migrated from tier identity to node, attempt, blocked episode, generation, lane, artifact, and provider-platform scopes.
items.title: Runtime identity modernization is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Tiers are demoted from primary Orchestrator tab/page authority in favor of Progress, Plan Compile, Seams, Node Graph, Evidence, History, and Ledger. Tier labels may survive only as derived presentation context or compatibility lineage. request_id and hitl_request_id are not durable graph action identity; blocked runtime approval identity, blocked_sequence, and allowed_action_ids-backed runtime actions own that role.

items.impact: Legacy tier and HITL identifiers cannot silently regain execution or mutation authority in the graph UI.
items.statement: The active tab model and blocked-action identity replace tier-era navigation and request identifiers, with legacy tokens constrained to compatibility lineage.
items.title: Tier and HITL compatibility authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Run Graph discloses stale or degraded projection trust before showing live claims, treats projection-trust failures and weak-integration findings as distinct concern categories, and gates actions that depend on current promotion, blocker, graph-generation, remote-side-effect truth, or cross-surface mutation payloads.

items.impact: Builders must decide when data becomes stale, which actions remain safe, how trust recovers, and how concurrent refreshes affect enabled controls, creating unsafe or misleading mutation affordances.
items.statement: Projection-trust disclosure and gating are mandatory, but trust-state enums, transition triggers, per-action gate outcomes, recovery rules, and observable error codes are not specified here.
items.title: Projection-trust gating is not executable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Run Graph records adjacent owner gaps without claiming non-local authority. Durable account switch history is already owned through account_switch_event and account_pressure_episode, while role enums, provider account policy references, acceptance/evidence/coverage schema extensions, and runtime scheduler ordering belong to their owner docs before Run Graph consumes them.

items.impact: Run Graph cannot deterministically consume role, provider-policy, coverage, or scheduler-ordering truth until owner contracts exist and are versioned, leaving cross-document integration and tests incomplete.
items.statement: The unit correctly refuses non-local authority but explicitly leaves several prerequisite owner contracts outside this document, without a consumed version, readiness condition, or compatibility behavior.
items.title: Adjacent owner contracts remain unresolved

evidence.exact_quote: - Route/open checks verify payload fidelity, owner routing, and missing context.

items.impact: Governance validators can pass while routing, projection trust, historical focus, stale-action gating, and large-graph behavior remain behaviorally unverified.
items.statement: Validation targets are named, but most are manual reviews or plan-governance scripts; no executable fixture matrix defines inputs, expected routes, trust states, disabled reasons, and failure outputs.
items.title: Validation lacks behavioral acceptance oracles

evidence.exact_quote: reusing live-run mode implicitly. Focus state persists as `orchestrator.project_state.{project_id}`

items.impact: Multiple tabs, restored sessions, active-run changes, or stale snapshots can overwrite one another or reopen an invalid node/attempt without a deterministic conflict or recovery path.
items.statement: Historical focus persistence is detailed, but revision ownership, atomic update semantics, concurrent-writer resolution, invalid restored selections, and offline revalidation are left open.
items.title: Historical focus persistence lacks conflict semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Run Graph must display GoalRun WorkGraph structure, WorkNode status, SubagentWave membership, VerificationCycle overlays, repair/retry markers, blocked/replan-required states, receipt refs, and evidence refs. For Plan/PlanUnit-originated graph preparation, the Node Graph and Run Graph views may show readiness, blockers, gui_related, receipt status, and compiler contract state only as projections. The view remains a projection over Goal Runtime, Executor, Contracts, storage, Plan_Document_System, and Plan_To_Node_Compilation records; it must not decide WorkNode readiness, capacity, compiler artifact creation, or completion authority.

items.impact: The view cannot legitimately mint readiness, capacity, dispatch, compiler artifacts, or completion truth while still exposing their owner-produced projections.
items.statement: GoalRun, WorkGraph, verification, and plan-preparation overlays have an explicit projection-only authority boundary against their runtime and compiler owners.
items.title: WorkGraph overlay authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote: Run Graph consumes plans-to-code execution progress after Executor intake by projecting queued WorkNodes, active WorkNodes, blocked WorkNodes, completed WorkNodes, dependency edges, model lanes, worktrees, safe points, test runs, browser/device sessions, repair loops, Auditor status, GitHub PR/Actions when configured, receipt refs, and final certification progress. The Run Graph remains an execution projection and does not own Plan Compile tab progress, PlanCompile state, Executor dispatch authority, or GoalCompletionReceipt certification authority.

items.impact: A node can appear completed while tests, receipts, GitHub state, safe points, or certification are stale or contradictory, with no specified precedence, watermark, partial-state marker, or rollback behavior.
items.statement: The execution projection aggregates many independently updating records but does not define correlation keys, ordering, snapshot consistency, source precedence, partial-availability semantics, or reconciliation after contradictory updates.
items.title: Execution progress has no consistency model

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Orchestrator Plan Compile tab shows immutable source pack, current stage, stage timeline, subagent assignments, PlanUnit coverage, NodeSeed candidates, WorkGraph status, WorkNodeRequest count, testing/model/source-control readiness, audit/repair cycles, blockers, receipts, and handoff status.'
Run Graph shows Executor execution progress only after intake and does not replace Plan Compile tab scope.

items.impact: A builder cannot tell whether to implement Plan Compile state and UI from Run Graph or its stated owner surfaces, risking duplicated state, divergent projections, and authority leakage across tabs.
items.statement: RGV-014 is owned by Run_Graph_View.md yet canonically specifies the Orchestrator Plan Compile tab, while RGV-013 says Run Graph does not replace Plan Compile scope; the consumption and ownership boundary is unresolved.
items.title: Plan Compile projection is placed under conflicting ownership

evidence.exact_quote: Run Graph usage and cost overlays consume UsageRecord projection packets. Node, attempt, edge, and detail-panel usage rows carry usage_event_ref, usage_record_id, provider_attempt_ref, attempt_id, node_id, tool_call_id, trace_ref, receipt refs, dedupe_key, parent_usage_record_id, source_class, source_confidence, source_authority, settlement_status, cost_status, quota_state, projection_freshness, projection_health, and counting_semantics where available. `View in Usage` routes by object_kind = usage_event and object_id from usage_event_ref; run_id, thread_id, tier_id, and timestamp remain filters, labels, or degraded fallback only.

items.impact: When usage_event_ref is absent, implementations can choose different fallback identities or silently open an ambiguous event, undermining route fidelity and cost trust despite the strong primary identity contract.
items.statement: UsageRecord identity and anti-double-counting requirements are strong, but the allowed degraded fallback lacks a deterministic priority, ambiguity rule, disabled reason, user disclosure, and recovery path.
items.title: Degraded usage routing is ambiguous

segments.summary: Reviewed the canonical Run Graph scope, host access evidence, live-versus-historical focus, and shared routing contract. Exact authority boundaries are strong; adversarial review found unresolved target-safety and route-payload semantics.

Reviewed layout scale, inspector disclosure, runtime identity migration, tier/HITL compatibility, projection trust, and adjacent owner routing. Identity and compatibility boundaries are explicit; performance, privacy, trust-state, and cross-owner contracts remain underdetermined.

Reviewed validation, historical focus persistence, WorkGraph overlays, execution progress, Plan Compile projection, and UsageRecord overlays. Projection authority is bounded, while executable oracles, concurrency, multi-source consistency, owner placement, and degraded usage routing remain open.
